Package index

Core

The harness for model calls, with or without a document: calls and clients, models and prices, context, effort, limits, caching and replay, composition and measurement. The groups follow the core guides in order, starting with vignette("core").

Calls, clients and results

One call to a model, the result it returns and the trace that records it. Clients for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, any provider ellmer supports, any function you write, and an offline stand-in for practice and tests. Signals a run records about its own work, and the schemas that check settings. See vignette("core").

hr_call()
Call a model
gr_result
The result of one model call
hr_client()
Construct a model client
hr_api_key()
Resolve the API key
hr_ellmer_client()
Read documents through an ellmer chat
hr_backend_client()
Use any function as the model transport
hr_mock_client()
A deterministic offline client for tests, demos and dry runs
hr_embed()
Embed texts
hr_trace() as.data.frame(<gr_trace>)
Create a run trace
hr_trace_summary()
Summarise a trace
hr_trace_cost()
What a run actually cost
hr_trace_save()
Save a trace to a file
as_json()
Serialise an object to JSON
hr_signal() hr_signals()
Record a self-signal
hr_param()
Declare one parameter of a module or spec
hr_schema() as.data.frame(<hr_schema>)
Collect parameters into a schema
hr_validate()
Validate and resolve settings against a schema

Models, prices and tokens

The model registry, the prices you set, cost estimates and token counts. See vignette("models").

hr_models()
List every known model
hr_model_info()
Look up a model's capabilities
hr_model_limits()
Context and output limits for a model
hr_register_model()
Register a model, or set the prices of a known one
hr_load_models()
Register models from a CSV file
hr_estimate_cost()
Estimate the USD cost of a set of calls
hr_count_tokens()
Count tokens in text
hr_tokenizer()
The active tokenizer
hr_set_tokenizer()
Register or inspect the active tokenizer

Context

How much room a prompt has, fitting its pieces into that room, and cutting one piece. See vignette("context").

hr_budget()
Compute a usable input-token budget for one model call
hr_context_fit()
Fit named pieces of text into a token budget under a context policy
hr_context_policy() print(<hr_context_policy>)
Rules for what a request keeps when its text does not fit
hr_truncate()
Cut text to a token count, keeping the part you choose
hr_truncate_tokens()
Truncate text to at most n tokens

Effort

Raising reasoning effort when a stage goes wrong, the log of each raise, and checking whether more effort pays. See vignette("effort").

hr_effort_escalate() print(<hr_effort_escalate>)
Reasoning effort that is raised for the next stage when a trigger fires
hr_effort_event()
Report a trigger for an effort escalation
hr_effort_log()
The effort raises of a run
hr_effort_check() print(<hr_effort_check>)
Compare an effort policy with fixed efforts on a benchmark

Limits, caching and replay

Settings and spending limits, paying for a request once, and replaying a recorded run without a model. See vignette("runs").

hr_options()
Get or set package options
hr_governor()
Limits on what a run may send
hr_cache()
A response cache
hr_cache_client()
Attach a cache to a client
hr_cache_stats()
Cache statistics
hr_cache_clear()
Delete every entry in a cache
hr_replay_client()
A client that answers from a recorded run

Compose steps and chains

Build a run from steps, run them in order as one arm, derive a chain by dropping or replacing a step, list, change and sweep its settings by path, give a step a skill, and check a step’s output by running a program. See vignette("compose").

hr_step()
A step of a run, with the settings it was built with
hr_chain()
Run steps in order as one arm
hr_settings()
List the settings of a step or a chain
hr_set()
Change some settings of a step or a chain
hr_step_command()
A step that runs a program
hr_skill()
Read a skill folder

Modules and the registry

Register and list modules of any kind, check a module against rules of your own, and declare what a module’s run costs. See “Registering a step” in vignette("compose"). “Declaring cost” in vignette("extending"), a document guide, covers hr_cost() with a reader.

hr_register()
Register a module of any kind
hr_modules()
List the registered modules of every kind
hr_check_module()
Check a module against a set of rules
hr_cost()
What one run of a module can cost

Benchmarks

Compare configurations on a labelled reference: arms, sweeps of a setting, the reference and its splits, scorers, and repeated runs held to one spending limit. See vignette("evaluate") and vignette("compare").

hr_benchmark() print(<hr_bench>)
Run arms against a reference
hr_report() print(<hr_bench_report>) as_json(<hr_bench_report>)
Report a benchmark with intervals
hr_error_correlation()
Correlated errors between the arms of a benchmark
hr_mdd() hr_n_needed() print(<hr_mdd>) print(<hr_n_needed>)
The minimum detectable difference of a paired, clustered design
hr_contrast() hr_register_contrasts() print(<hr_contrast>) print(<hr_contrast_registration>)
Non-inferiority contrasts, registered before scoring
hr_drift_check() print(<hr_drift_check>)
Check an arm for drift against a frozen benchmark
hr_arm()
A configuration to compare in a benchmark
hr_sweep()
Build one arm per row of a grid of settings
hr_sweep_check()
Find the settings of a sweep that changed nothing that was sent
hr_reference() hr_reference_add()
A reference set to score arms against
hr_scorer() hr_scorer_exact()
A rule for scoring an arm's output
hr_assign_splits()
Assign reference items to splits by cluster

Judges

A model that chooses between candidates or grades one against a reference, asked in both orders, validated against blind human labels before it scores, with its accuracy corrected by those labels. See vignette("evaluate").

hr_judge() print(<hr_judgement>)
Judge candidates with a model, in more than one order
hr_judge_config() print(<hr_judge_config>)
A judge configuration
hr_judge_validate() hr_judge_valid() print(<hr_judge_validation>)
Validate a judge against blind human labels
hr_scorer_judge()
Score benchmark runs with a validated judge
hr_judge_ppi()
Judge-scored accuracy corrected with human labels

Baselines

Comparisons that use no model: tf-idf features, a cross-fitted classifier and a simulated active-learning ranker for screening. See vignette("evaluate").

hr_tfidf()
Tf-idf features from texts
hr_baseline_classifier() print(<hr_baseline_classifier>)
Cross-fitted text classifier baseline
hr_baseline_ranker() print(<hr_baseline_ranker>)
Active-learning screening baseline

Signal calibration

The calibration records that measure how well a signal predicts being right, and the thresholds and policy that decide whether a signal may gate an action. Nothing gates by default. See vignette("evaluate").

hr_calibrate_signal()
Calibrate a self-signal against graded items
hr_calibration_valid()
Is a calibration record valid for a run?
hr_gate_threshold()
Choose a gate threshold by Learn-then-Test
hr_signal_policy() hr_apply_signal()
What a signal may do, and what happens when it may not

Statistics

Intervals for proportions, agreement between raters and coders, design- weighted and prediction-powered estimates, and the test of whether a model’s labels can stand in for people’s. See vignette("evaluate").

hr_prop_ci()
Confidence intervals for binomial proportions
hr_agreement()
Agreement between raters, with every measure that should go with it
hr_ht_estimate()
Design-weighted estimates from a probability sample
hr_ppi()
Prediction-powered inference for a mean
hr_alt_test()
The alternative annotator test

Documents

The document layer, built on the core: ingest, segment, read, and review many documents. See vignette("harnessr") for a first question.

Ask a question

One call reads a document and answers a question, and the answer says what it rests on and whether anything went wrong. See vignette("harnessr").

answer_document()
Answer a question about a document
gr_answer
The result of one reading run
is_not_found()
Did the model report that the document does not contain the answer?
gr_example()
Path to the bundled example document
gr_recipes()
Ready-made recipes
gr_recipe()
Bind an ingestion, segmentation and reading configuration together
gr_compare()
Run several recipes over one document and compare them
gr_methods_text()
A methods paragraph from a run's record

Get text out of files

Extraction, cleaning and a survey of a folder before anything is spent. See vignette("ingest").

gr_extractors()

gr_cleaners()

gr_clean()
Run the cleaning pipeline over a character vector
gr_inventory()
What is in a folder, before you read any of it
gr_flush_caches()
Clear the session's document and embedding caches

Cut documents into chunks

The segmenters, their settings, and the free statistics for comparing chunkings: size, boundary error against a reference (Pk and WindowDiff) and retrieval recall. See vignette("segment") and vignette("compare").

gr_segment_spec()

gr_seg_boundaries()
Where a segmentation puts its boundaries, sentence by sentence
gr_seg_pk() gr_seg_windowdiff()

gr_seg_recall()
Retrieval recall at k, per segmenter

Read the chunks

The reading strategies, the settings that choose and place chunks, the embedders that rank them, and the check on quoted evidence. See vignette("readers").

gr_read()

List registered reading strategies

gr_embedders()
List registered embedding backends
gr_verify_evidence()
Check that quoted evidence really is in the document

Many documents and literature reviews

One question over many documents, and a review from a search export to screened studies, an extraction table, a written review and an audit report, with the screening measured against a hand-screened sample and a stopping test for prioritised screening. See vignette("review").

Document arms, steps and references

Document arms and steps for the core benchmarks and chains, question- answer references, label sheets, and the checks on what a reader keeps. See vignette("evaluate") and vignette("compose").

gr_step() gr_step_retrieve()

gr_label_sheet()

Settings of the document stages

The settings of a read, segment or ingest spec, and every setting of every stage in one table. See vignette("settings").

gr_settings()
The settings of a read, segment or ingest spec
gr_settings_table()
Every setting of every stage

Extending the document layer

Every document axis is a registry, and an addition is used exactly like a built-in. Register extractors, cleaners, segmenters, readers and embedders, build the objects they return, and check them against the contract. See vignette("extending").

gr_register_extractor()
Register a document extractor
gr_register_cleaner()
Register a cleaning step
gr_register_segmenter()
Register a segmentation strategy
gr_register_reader()
Register a reading strategy
gr_register_embedder()
Register an embedding backend
new_chunks()
Build a gr_chunks, the object every segmenter must return
new_answer()
Build a gr_answer, the object every reader must return
gr_check_reader()
Check a reader against the reader contract
gr_check_segmenter()
Check a segmenter against the segmenter contract
